content.text:
There are three levels of protection. Only the last one actually guarantees it.

**1. Deny rules (what Code and Ask already get for the spec).** Pass `--disallowedTools "Read(/…/src/**),Edit(/…/src/**),Write(/…/src/**),Glob(/…/src/**),Grep(/…/src/**)"`. This is cheap, but it's still only a nudge, because Bash can `cat src/foo.rs`. The agent also burns tokens hitting the denials and working around them.

**2. Deny rules plus no free Bash.** A spec step only really needs Bash to run `piton build`. You can either:
- drop Bash from its tools and have the harness run `piton build` after the step, sending any errors back as a fed message; or
- allow only `Bash(piton build*)`. Check how this interacts with `--permission-mode auto`, because auto mode may let other commands through.

That shuts the obvious routes, but it's still a list of rules the agent can get around (subagents, `piton slice` on a code target, and so on), and it relies on Claude Code's own enforcement.

**3. Run the step where the code doesn't exist (the absolute option).** Run the spec step inside a mount namespace that hides the code, so it isn't there to see:

```
bwrap --bind / / --tmpfs /…/project/src --dev /dev --proc /proc -- claude -p …
```

The process sees an empty `src/`. Reads, Bash, subagents, every tool and every harness (Codex and OpenCode too) all get nothing. Nothing is denied, so the agent wastes no tokens on refusals. It also replaces the mode guard for Spec and chain step 1, because edits there are impossible rather than reverted afterwards.

Things to check if you go this way:
- **Linux only.** macOS would need `sandbox-exec` or an equivalent profile, and Windows has no simple equivalent, so keep level 1 as the fallback there.
- **Your `codeRoot` must not contain the spec or `.claude/reference`.** In this repo it doesn't: `src/` is separate from `spec/` and `.claude/`.
- **Shape files are hidden too.** Shape instructions compile into `src/**/CLAUDE.md`, so those vanish as well. A spec agent shouldn't need them, but the reference copy is still under `.claude/reference`.
- **Claude Code's built-in sandbox.** It may be able to do this natively with its own sandbox and filesystem deny-read settings, which would avoid wrapping the binary. I'm not sure it applies a read deny to Bash in `-p` mode, so it would need testing before relying on it.

**Whichever level you pick, stop pointing the agent at the code.** Today the system prompt and the Combined instructions both name `${CODE_LOCATION}`. For Spec mode and chain step 1, describe the code only as "not yours to read or change", or not at all. An agent told where the code is will go and look.

**Recommendation:** use level 3 (bwrap) for Spec and chain step 1 on Linux, with level 1 rules as the fallback elsewhere, and remove the code location from those prompts. I can turn that into a Chain prompt if you want.
